description: Single authoritative role->tool access policy for the wiki-mcp server (WK-1492#SLICE-001). Each entry in `access` maps a registered agent-reachable tool name to the session roles allowed to call it. This file is the ONE access source: fail-closed by construction, a tool omitted for a role (or omitted from `access` entirely) is denied to that role. The role gate composes as an independent AND with the product-tier gate AND the per-tool install_state=installed + runtime_posture=supported co-gating (both stay in the tool-discovery descriptor); this policy carries access only, never tier or install/runtime posture. Classification follows WK-1492 acceptance criteria 3-4: CONTENT read/inspect/navigation tools are broad to the advisory roles (orchestrator+reviewer+redteam); PROCESS/dispatch-measurement reads (validate_dispatch, coordination_preflight, initiative_status, integration_status, agent_run_status, agent_run_wait, node_engine_admission_runtime_diagnostic) and ALL action/authority tools are orchestrator-only, because a role that can measure process (dispatchability, admission, coordination, run monitoring) will grade process, which is the orchestrator's job; the closed-input `commit` primitive is worker; workspace_submit_for_review is reviewer+redteam; explicit code/search cache build tools and operator observability are operator-only, while validate_dispatch retains its existing orchestrator/operator access and may refresh only its ignored current-HEAD graph cache, atomic temp, persistent advisory lock, and eight bounded candidate slots; operator is the full surface. The two server-local tools (`commit`, `workspace_submit_for_review`) carry real descriptor inventory entries in mcp-tools.json (free_local tier); their ACCESS is this policy, and the inventory carries no roles field. The completeness/dangling/known-role guard lives in packages/wiki-core/src/operations/lint.mjs. WK-1512#SLICE-013 (DEC-0152/DEC-0155): conferring or removing `accepted` decision authority is not an MCP capability for ANY role, operator included - workspace_decision_ratify/workspace_decision_unratify are unregistered and absent from this policy, and the human `wiki decision ratify`/`wiki decision unratify` CLI is the sole accepted-authority transition surface. Agents keep only the proposed lane (workspace_decision_create, workspace_decision_amend_section, workspace_decision_amend_scalar, workspace_decision_reject).

role_descriptions.orchestrator: Coordinator surface: all CONTENT reads plus the process/dispatch-measurement reads (validate_dispatch, coordination_preflight, initiative_status, integration_status, agent_run_status, agent_run_wait, node_engine_admission_runtime_diagnostic) and the action/authority tools (dispatch, work_record_* setters, create_record, generate_and_lint/lint/docs hygiene, run_validation, review-recording). Not commit, not submit_for_review.
role_descriptions.reviewer: Findings-only reviewer: broad CONTENT read/inspect/navigation surface plus workspace_submit_for_review. No process-measurement, mutation, or authority tools.
role_descriptions.worker: Managed implementation worker: exactly the closed-input commit primitive (the worker reads via its sandboxed filesystem, not wiki-mcp); trusted integration freezes the later review target.
role_descriptions.redteam: Findings-only redteam: same broad CONTENT read surface as reviewer plus workspace_submit_for_review. No process-measurement, mutation, or authority tools.
role_descriptions.operator: Full surface: every registered agent-reachable tool, including cache writers and operator-only observability.
